evidence: Her foot caught the edge of the bath mat and she sat down on the floor. The care worker lowered her gently. She did not hit her head.
summary: E.W. caught her foot on a bath mat and sat down on the floor while walking to the bathroom with a care worker. No injury or pain. GP reviewed, no treatment needed. Non-slip mat replaced.

evidence: Staff called police at 15:30 and reported R.T. missing.
summary: R.T. left the unit through a gate propped open by a contractor. Police were called and found him 2 km away, cold and confused but unhurt.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: M.K. said "he grabbed me hard last night when I didn't want to get up". One care worker assisted M.K. with a transfer at about 02:00.
summary: Staff found new bruising on both of M.K.'s forearms. M.K. alleged a care worker grabbed her hard during a 02:00 transfer. GP examined and prescribed pain relief and dressings. Care worker stood down pending investigation.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: J.P.'s daughter reported four cash withdrawals totalling $240 from her father's bank card between 1 and 10 October. J.P. has not left the facility this month. The card is kept in the facility safe. The safe access log shows one staff member opened it on each of the four days.
summary: Resident's daughter reported four unauthorised cash withdrawals totalling $240 from resident's bank card. Safe access log shows one staff member opened the safe on each occasion. Staff member stood down.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: The night agency nurse raised both bed rails for D.L. overnight "to stop him wandering". D.L. has no assessment, consent or behaviour support plan for bed rails.
summary: Agency nurse raised both bed rails overnight to prevent wandering without required assessment, consent, or behaviour support plan. Rails lowered at 06:00. No injury or distress.

evidence: At lunch she was served a regular-texture roast. She coughed on the first mouthful and staff removed the meal at once.
summary: Resident requiring minced and moist meals was served a regular-texture roast. She coughed on the first mouthful. Staff removed the meal and a RN checked her. No treatment was needed.
